1.statement:
**What to build.** Code in the editor that opens the registration form, fills the First Name,
Last Name, and Address fields with values of your own, and shows a screenshot.

**Where.** In the editor, using `launch()` and `show(page)`.

**How you will know it worked.** The screenshot shows your three values in their fields, and the
Console tab shows no error.

**Hint.** The two name fields have placeholder text. The Address field is the only `textarea` on
the page.

2.statement:
**What to build.** A test of your own that uses the helper. In the `tests` folder, create
`practice-register.spec.ts`, with one test that imports `fillRegistrationForm` from
`'./registration-helpers'`, calls it with an email of your own, and checks that the Email field
holds that email.

**Where.** In VS Code and its integrated terminal. Copy your test and the result into the editor,
using the template.

**How you will know it worked.** The run reports `1 passed`, and your test contains no `fill()`
line of its own.

**Hint.** Start from the first test in [Implementation](/learn/w2/d1/p3), and change the email in
both places.

3.statement:
**What to build.** A helper that also takes the phone number. In the `tests` folder:

1. In `registration-helpers.ts`, give `fillRegistrationForm` a third parameter, `phone`, and
   fill the Phone field with it. Give the parameter a default value of `'5551234567'`, so that
   `register-helper.spec.ts` still works without a change. A **default value** is written after
   `=` in the parameter list, and it is used when a call leaves that parameter out.
2. Create `practice-phone.spec.ts`, with one test that calls the helper with an email and a phone
   number of your own, and checks that the Phone field holds that number.
3. Run both spec files in one command:
   `npx playwright test tests/register-helper.spec.ts tests/practice-phone.spec.ts --project=chromium`.

**Where.** In VS Code and its integrated terminal. Copy the changed function, your new test, and
the result into the editor, using the template.

**How you will know it worked.** The run reports `3 passed`: the two tests that call the helper
with an email only, and your test that also passes a phone number.

**Hint.** The Phone field is the `<input>` whose `type` attribute is `tel`.
